title: Oklahoma's 14 Straight Conference Titles, 1946-1959
question: How many straight conference championships did Oklahoma win under Bud Wilkinson?
answer: Oklahoma won 14 straight conference titles from 1946 through 1959, 13 of them under Bud Wilkinson (1947-1959). The 1946 title came under Jim Tatum, and Wilkinson inherited the run in his first season.
summary: Oklahoma won 14 straight conference titles from 1946 to 1959, 13 under Bud Wilkinson. See how the streak began, who started it and when it ended.
body: Oklahoma's conference dominance in the 1940s and 1950s is one of the most lopsided runs in college football. The Sooners won a conference championship every season from 1946 through 1959, a streak of 14 straight, according to a Sports Illustrated look back at OU's league titles.

The run actually began before Bud Wilkinson arrived. Jim Tatum's 1946 team shared the Big Six title, and Wilkinson's first team in 1947 shared it again. Those first two crowns were not clean sweeps, but what followed was close to perfect.

From 1948 through 1958 the Sooners won the league outright every year. Oklahoma's conference records in those seasons were unbeaten, including a 7-0 mark in 1958, per the program's season-by-season table. Over Wilkinson's 13 straight titles, 1947 through 1959, Oklahoma lost just one conference game and tied two, according to Storm in Norman's rewind of the era.

The streak overlapped with the 47-game winning streak of 1953 to 1957 and the national championships of 1950, 1955 and 1956. It finally ended in 1960, when the Sooners went 2-4-1 in league play and finished fifth.
Fans sometimes quote the number as 13, and that is correct for Wilkinson's own tenure. Counting Tatum's 1946 co-championship, the unbroken string is 14.
